sections.content: How many people are "ship and hovercraft officers"?

9,290 people

were counted on the census as "ship and hovercraft officers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Ship and hovercraft officers command and navigate ships and other craft, co-ordinate the activities of officers and deck and engine room ratings, operate and maintain communications equipment on board ship and undertake minor repairs to engines, boilers and other mechanical and electrical equipment.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "ship and hovercraft officers" there were more men than women (93.7% compared with 6.3%).

This means "ship and hovercraft officers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 93.8% and women made up 6.2% of "ship and hovercraft officers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "ship and hovercraft officers" included:

  • telecoms and related network installers and repairers
  • electrical and electronic trades (other)
  • pest control officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "ship and hovercraft officers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "ship and hovercraft officers", 13.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "ship and hovercraft officers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "ship and hovercraft officers" included:

  • publicans and managers of licensed premises
  • estimators, valuers and assessors
  • biological scientists

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "ship and hovercraft officers", 5.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (91.2% compared with 8.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (88.1%) than self-employed (11.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
